title: Moriches
summary: Moriches is a south-shore Brookhaven placename connected with a neck of land at Unquichoge and with the later hamlets of Moriches, Center Moriches, and East Moriches. Early forms include Merquices and Meritche.
map_geometry_source: approximate modern Center Moriches / Moriches Bay area marker; offset slightly for map visibility
introduction_content: Moriches names a south-shore landscape in eastern Brookhaven. In William Wallace Tooker's placename study, the name is tied to a neck of land at Unquichoge and to later village names along Moriches Bay.
history_content: Moriches neck, the later hamlet names, and related Moriches Bay geography are brought together here. Time-specific land-title context is handled as a Historic Moment.
translation_content:
Alternate forms include Merquices and Meritche. The meaning of Meritche is uncertain; the history discusses a personal-name compound glossed as Meritche's old woman, with the old-woman element compared to Montauk and Narragansett forms.

Why Place Names Matter

“If place names are left undocumented then the owners and history of those places remain invisible. Place names provide clear evidence of land use and demonstrate Native presence in an area.”

— Gary Holton, Statement quoted in Mapping Traditional Place Names along the Koyukuk River—Koyukuk, Huslia, and Hughes, Western Interior Alaska (2014), USGS Fact Sheet 2014–3105, PDF page 1
whereintheworld_content: The point is an approximate general marker near Center Moriches and Moriches Bay, chosen to represent the broader Moriches placename area rather than an exact historic boundary. It is offset slightly from nearby Moriches-area placename pins for map visibility.
